title: Burst Balloons
description:
You are given n balloons, indexed from 0 to n - 1. Each balloon is painted with a number on it represented by an array nums. You are asked to burst all the balloons.

If you burst the ith balloon, you will get nums[i - 1] * nums[i] * nums[i + 1] coins. If i - 1 or i + 1 goes out of bounds of the array, then treat it as if there is a balloon with a 1 painted on it.

Return the maximum coins you can collect by bursting the balloons wisely.

examples.explanation: Burst 1 first for 1*1*5 = 5, then 5 for 1*5*1 = 5, total 10.

approach: Pad the array with boundary 1s so every subproblem is an open interval (left, right). Let dp[left][right] be the most coins obtainable by bursting all balloons strictly between left and right. If k is the LAST balloon burst inside that interval, its final gain is values[left] * values[k] * values[right] (its only remaining neighbors are the untouched boundaries), and the two sides dp[left][k] and dp[k][right] are independent subproblems. Trying every k over all O(n^2) intervals gives O(n^3) time and O(n^2) space.
